newsitem.title: TURKEY: U.N. envoy visits Turkey after Cyprus incident.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy visits Turkey after Cyprus incident.

text.p: A United Nations envoy to Cyprus arrived in Istanbul on Thursday for talks with Turkish officials as U.N. forces on the divided island investigated a shooting incident between Greek and Turkish Cypriots.
State-run Anatolian news agency said envoy Han Sung-Joo declined to comment on the incident, which according to U.N. information involved shooting by both sides. There were no reports of injuries.

"The U.N. is presenting an important opportunity for the two communities to reach agreement with one another. Both communities must use this opportunity," Han told reporters on arrival at Istanbul airport.

But he said there must be more consultation before leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities held direct talks. Han held separate discussions with the two leaders on the Mediterranean island this week and said more work was needed to narrow the differences.
He is to hold talks on Friday with Turkey's Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller and leading Foreign Ministry officials.
Ciller, who is also foreign minister, earlier called the shooting in Cyprus a provocation but said Turkey would respond with "cool-headedness," the semi-official Anatolian news agency said.

Opposing sides on the island gave different accounts of the incident, which took place in the middle of the night 20 km (12 miles) southeast of Nicosia. Turkey said infiltrators had tried to remove a Turkish flag, the Cypriot government denied any knowledge of shooting.
U.N. troops man a buffer zone that has divided the island since Turkey invaded the north in 1974 after a Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia engineered by the military then in power in Greece.

Decades of international efforts to reunite the island under a federal umbrella have failed and the dispute remains a source of tension between NATO partners Greece and Turkey. NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana was in Ankara on Thursday for talks that covered relations between the two countries.
